label: first early occurrence of a token from {g,r,j,y,u,t,3,s,i,e,p,v} in the original phase (t<=2)
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires at the start of the original sequence on the first input from a specific token set. At t=0 it fires with precision 1.0 exactly when the input is one of g,r,j,y,u,t,3,s,i,e,p,v; this holds about 75% of activation mass. At t=1-2 it fires only for the stronger subset g,r,j,y,u,t,3, and only if no token from the 12-token set has appeared yet. An earlier set token suppresses it (e.g. y then r: r is inactive). Magnitude depends on the token (g > r > j > y,u,t > 3 > s,i,e,p; v sits right at threshold) and drops sharply with position (t=0 >> t=1 > t=2, with a small tail at t=3-4). It never fires at t>=5 or on repeated tokens (in_first=0), and almost never in the copy phase (1% of mass, at steps L+1/L+2 re-inputting an early set token). Exception, not covered by the predicate: the single largest activations are on <DEL> in L=3 sequences, mostly ones containing no set token (e.g. k 2 f <DEL>). The delimiter holds about 3.5% of mass. Dev: P 0.88, R 0.90, F1 0.89, mass recall 0.94.

issues: The core story holds up. At t=0 the predicate (phase==0)&(t==0)&in_tok in the 12-token set has precision 1.000 and mass recall 0.755. An earlier set token does suppress the unit: at t=1-2 with seen(set), precision is 0.077.

Systematic false positives at t=2. The predicate at t=2 has precision only 0.524. Per-token precision at t=2 with no earlier set token falls steadily: g 0.875, r 0.722, j 0.557, y 0.472, u 0.412, t 0.376, 3 0.257. So 'fires for the stronger subset g,r,j,y,u,t,3 at t=1-2' overclaims at t=2 for u, t and 3, which are mostly inactive there. At t=1, token 3 is also only 0.48.

Systematic misses at the delimiter. In L=3 sequences, (phase==1)&(L==3) is active 68% of the time (97% when no set token has appeared). The explanation mentions this exception, but the predicate leaves it out, and it is a clean, predictable class.
Small factual error. 'A small tail at t=3-4' is really the <DEL> step of L=3/L=4 sequences. In the original phase at t=3-4 the unit is essentially silent (precision 0.002, mass 0.2%).
The remaining gaps are graded, not a different mechanism. Activation falls with t and with token rank, so the hard t<=2 cutoff with a fixed token set is a coarse fit.
skeptic.revised_label: First occurrence of a token from {g,r,j,y,u,t,3,s,i,e,p,v} at the very start of the original sequence. At t=0 any set token fires it; at t=1 only g,r,j,y,u,t,3; at t=2 only g,r,j. It also fires on <DEL> in L=3 sequences.
